newsitem.title: BULGARIA: South Korea's Daewoo expands Bulgaria operations.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's Daewoo expands Bulgaria operations.

text.p: South Korean conglomerate Daewoo Corp on Thursday announced plans to step up its presence in Bulgaria, whose crumbling economy is in dire need of foreign investment.
Daewoo said it had set up a Bulgarian subsidiary and was looking at buying a bank, bidding for a mobile telephone contract and taking a stake in a forklift truck producer.
"Daewoo Corp is setting up Daewoo Bulgaria AD as a part of its strategy for expansion in this country," the head of Daewoo's Sofia branch office Chung-Hwan Kim told a news conference.
"We are interested in Bulgaria's banking sector, chemical industry, telecommunications, machine building and tourism."
Young-Kwan Kwon, managing director of the new company, said Daewoo planned to produce forklift trucks in Bulgaria.
"We are going to hold talks with Bulgarian officials on buying a stake in the state-owned forklift truck producer Balkankar Holding or setting up a joint venture," Kwon said.
He said long-term projects also included production of car parts and their export to third countries.
Daewoo's investment plans come at a time when the debt-ridden Balkan country is battling severe economic crisis.
International lenders have criticised the Socialist government for not doing enough to attract foreign funds.
Foreign investors complain of excessive bureaucracy, delays in privatisation, unclear and arbitrarily enforced rules and rampant organised crime.

In April, a car making joint venture between Rover Group Ltd, a subsidiary of German automaker Bayerische Motoren Werke AG, and a Bulgarian consortium, closed down citing bureaucratic obstacles and lack of government support.
Rodacar said the government had ignored its pleas for tax breaks and a new trade deal with the Czech Republic meant imported Skodas were cheaper than cars assembled in Bulgaria.

"The economic situation in Bulgaria is unstable and not quite clear...Nevertheless, we are committed to stepping up our activities here...We will be happy to contribute to the country's economic reforms," Kim said.
Asked how much Daewoo planned to invest in Bulgaria, Kim said the company had set no particular limit and spending would depend on the exact enterprises which were developed.
He said Daewoo was considering buying one of the country's troubled banks to service its expansion.
"We would like to have a Bulgarian registered bank...because of our expanded activities here," Kim said.
"We discussed the matter with (Bulgaria's) cabinet and they recommended to us Balkanbank."
Balkanbank is one of nine local commercial banks placed under special supervision last month in a bid to stabilise the country's crumbling financial system.
Of the nine, Balkanbank has the highest level of personal and company deposits and it posted a cumulative loss of 9.3 billion levs up to the end of August this year.
Daewoo said it was also interested in Bulgaria's plans to sell a stake in the state telecommunication company and would bid for a second GSM operator contract if the government launched a tender.
Daewoo established an office in Bulgaria in 1992. Last month it bought a 67 percent stake in Sofia's luxury Sheraton Hotel and pledged to invest some $5 million in it over the next five years.
